rationale: C22 is a direct predecessor and an unmistakable drafting template. The child repeats the same event, sponsor, congressional-recognition framework, substantive themes of scientific exchange and metal-resource conservation, and nearly the entire operative paragraph verbatim, changing principally the congress number, date, location, and factual emphasis. C20 and C19 share some recognition or international-congress machinery, but neither approaches C22's literal and structural correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Second World Metallurgical Congress to be held at Chicago, Illinois, from November 2 to November 8, 1957, under the sponsorship of the American Society for Metals
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the World Metallurgical Congress to be held at Detroit, Michigan, from October 14 to 19, 1951, under the sponsorship of the American Society for Metals
shared_material.explanation: The same sponsored congress is described through an event template adapted to its second occurrence, with updated city and dates.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the free exchange of scientific information among the metallurgists of the world and stimulate the search for minerals and for improved techniques in the field of metallurgy
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the exchange among scientists of the free world of scientific knowledge and industrial techniques in the field of metallurgy
shared_material.explanation: Both use closely parallel language to justify the congress through international exchange of metallurgical knowledge and techniques.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the need for the conservation of our present resources and for the discovery and development of new sources of supply
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the conservation of available metal resources and the discovery and development of additional sources of supply
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive shared substantive language concerning conservation and development of metal supplies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby extend recognition to the Second World Metallurgical Congress and commend the American Society for Metals for initiating and sponsoring this meeting. I also extend the welcome of this Government to the Congress and to the scientists attending its proceedings, and I request that all Federal departments and agencies assist and cooperate with the Second World Metallurgical Congress as occasion may warrant.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby extend recognition to the World Metallurgical Congress and commend the American Society for Metals for initiating and sponsoring this meeting. I also extend the welcome of this Government to the Congress and to the scientists attending its proceedings, and I request that all Federal departments and agencies assist and cooperate with the World Metallurgical Congress as occasion may warrant.
shared_material.explanation: The operative provisions are virtually verbatim, with only the addition of “Second” to the congress name.
